meta.title: Discovery Timeline
meta.note: One entry per find. foundDate is the date the research found the record, not the date of the event. This file stays in step with data/discoveries.json, which is the canonical discoveries list for a later engine release. The 1.0.1 site pages still read this file.

finds.headline: Pat Fucale's obituary names his wife and the Vigliotti in-laws
finds.summary: The Ballard-Durand obituary for Pasquale "Pat" Fucale (22 September 1952 to 21 November 2026) records his 1977 marriage to a daughter of the Eastchester Vigliotti family, and names her brother and sister, with their spouses, as his in-laws.

finds.headline: The Walsh obituary names their daughter and her parents
finds.summary: The Rye Record obituary of Patricia Morrisey Walsh and Paul H. Walsh, published 14 October 2019, names their daughter and her husband, and gives Patricia and Paul's own parents, marriage on 5 May 1951, and deaths in September 2019.

finds.headline: Alphonse Vigliotti Sr.'s obituary names his parents and children
finds.summary: The 2011 Journal News obituary of Alphonse J. Vigliotti Sr. (14 March 1921 to 1 January 2011), transcribed on Find a Grave, names his parents Vincent Vigliotti and Vencenza Guido, a son, two daughters, and grandchildren.

finds.headline: WWII draft card gives Alphonse Sr.'s birth date and father
finds.summary: Alphonse John Vigliotti registered at Tuckahoe on 15 February 1942, born 14 March 1921 at Scarsdale, New York, naming Vincent Vigliotti as the person who would always know his address.

finds.headline: The Vigliotti household at 44 Brambach Avenue, Eastchester
finds.summary: The 1930 and 1940 censuses show Vincent and Vincenza Vigliotti, both born in Italy, with their children including Alphonse, at 44 Brambach Avenue, Eastchester.

finds.headline: Four Vigliotti sons in the service, 1942
finds.summary: The Scarsdale Inquirer of 4 December 1942 reported that Mr. and Mrs. Vincent Vigliotti of Brambach Road had four sons in the armed forces and had just marked 25 years of marriage.

finds.headline: Vincent Vigliotti's death in 1944
finds.summary: The New York State death index (indexed as VIGHIOTTO) and the Scarsdale Inquirer record the death of Vincent J. Vigliotti, aged 53, at Grasslands Hospital, Mount Pleasant, on 24 April 1944.

finds.headline: Alphonse Vigliotti marries Concetta Mignone, 1947
finds.summary: The Scarsdale Inquirer announced the engagement (4 April 1947) and the 24 August 1947 wedding at Immaculate Heart of Mary, Scarsdale, of Concetta, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Gerard Mignone, and Alphonse J., son of Mrs. Vincent Vigliotti.

finds.headline: Another researcher's tree points to Santa Maria a Vico and Arienzo
finds.summary: An Ancestry member tree first pointed to Vincenzo Vigliotti's birth as 4 July 1885 at Santa Maria a Vico and Vincenza Pasqualina Guida's as 21 September 1899 at Arienzo, and named their parents. The civil birth acts have now been read and confirm those dates and towns.

finds.headline: Vincenzo Vigliotti arrives on the Roma, 1903
finds.summary: A New York passenger list index shows Vincenzo Vigliotti, aged 17, arriving at New York on the ship Roma on 1 April 1903. The manifest page itself was later read; see the separate find for that reading.

finds.headline: Gerard Mignone, Concetta's father
finds.summary: The Scarsdale Inquirer obituary of Gerard Mignone (died 29 October 1957), the 1950 census and the Westchester naturalization index (1923 declaration, 1929 petition) identify Concetta's parents as Gerard and Susan (Rescigno) Mignone.

finds.headline: Paul Walsh and Patricia Morrisey wed in Scarsdale, 1951
finds.summary: The Scarsdale Inquirer reported the engagement (19 January 1951) and the 5 May 1951 wedding of Patricia Morrissey, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. James T. Morrissey of Downer Avenue, and Paul H. Walsh, son of former Mayor and Mrs. William A. Walsh of Yonkers.

finds.headline: Barbara's great grandmother Augusta Ehrenfels
finds.summary: The Scarsdale Inquirer of 17 June 1949 reports the death of Mrs. Augusta R. Ehrenfels of Mount Vernon, mother of Mrs. James Morrissey.

finds.headline: Barbara's grandfather was Mayor of Yonkers
finds.summary: Paul Walsh's wedding notice calls his father "former Mayor" William A. Walsh of Yonkers; William A. Walsh (1871 to 1967) was Mayor of Yonkers 1926 to 1927, and Social Security records name William A. Walsh and Clara Hingston as parents of children born in Yonkers in 1914 and 1917.

finds.headline: The Walsh line goes back to Ardmore, Ireland
finds.summary: The 1916 Yonkers Statesman obituary of Michael Walsh, father of Mayor William A. Walsh, says he was born in Ardmore, Ireland, came to America as a boy, and built a carpentry business in Yonkers.

finds.headline: Clara Hingston's family came from Huntingdon, Quebec
finds.summary: Catherine Jane Cleary Hingston's 1932 obituary names her parents Owen and Catherine Donohue Cleary of Huntingdon, Canada, her 1872 marriage to Samuel J. Hingston, and her daughter Mrs. William A. Walsh.

finds.headline: James Morrisey and Fernanda Ehrenfels married in 1922
finds.summary: The Westchester County marriage index lists James T. Morrisey and Fernanda Ehrenfels on the same certificate, number 37675, in 1922.

finds.headline: Gerardo Mignone and Susan Rescigno married in 1926
finds.summary: The Westchester County marriage index lists Gerardo Mignone and Susan M. Rescigno on certificate 51289 in 1926.

finds.headline: 1920 census: Vincent Vigliotti had filed first papers
finds.summary: The January 1920 census lists Vincent Vigliotte, 34, on Scarsdale Avenue, Eastchester, immigrated 1902, with citizenship Pa, meaning he had declared his intention but was not yet a citizen. His wife Vincenza, 20, had arrived in 1916.

finds.headline: 1925 census: a citizen since 1923, White Plains
finds.summary: The June 1925 New York State census at 44 Brambach Avenue marks the head of the Vigliotti household a citizen, with the note 1923 White Plains, and lists sons Vincent, Alfonso, Andrew and Anthony and daughter Madeline.

finds.headline: Vincenzo's naturalization papers found under misspellings
finds.summary: The Westchester County naturalization index has a 1916 declaration for Vincenzo Viglietto and a 1922 petition for Vincenzo Vigletti (Viglotti). With the census trail, this points to naturalization in 1922 or 1923, after Alphonse Sr. was born in March 1921. The 1928 and 1930 papers in the same index belong to a different Vincenzo, born in 1892 at Bonito.

finds.headline: The Roma manifest: a 17 year old farm labourer joining a cousin
finds.summary: On the S.S. Roma manifest for 1 April 1903, a 17-year-old single farm labourer whose surname is only partly readable, paid his own passage, carried $20, and was going to a cousin at 312 Broadway, Newburgh, New York.

finds.headline: Vincenzo's Italian birth act: 4 July 1885, Santa Maria a Vico
finds.summary: The civil birth register of Santa Maria a Vico shows that Vincenzo Vigliotti was born at 11 at night on 4 July 1885, at Via Rusciano 23, to Andrea Vigliotti, a 32-year-old farmer, and his wife Mariantonia Ruotolo. His father registered the birth the next morning. This settles his birth date and town.

finds.headline: Vincenza was a twin, born in Arienzo in 1899
finds.summary: Vincenza Pasqualina Guida was born at 11:40 in the morning on 21 September 1899 at via Maddalena 2, Arienzo, the first of twins born to Alfonso Guida, a 33-year-old farmer, and Antonia Vigliotti. Her twin brother, Pasquale Fabrizio, was born second and recorded in the next act.

finds.headline: Vincenza lost her mother at four: Antonia Vigliotti, died 1904
finds.summary: Antonia Vigliotti, wife of Alfonso Guida, died at Arienzo on 8 June 1904, aged 38. Her death act says she was born in San Felice a Cancello, the daughter of Raffaele Vigliotti, a farmer, and Pasqualina Carfora.

finds.headline: One generation further back: Andrea Vigliotti, born 1853
finds.summary: The 1853 birth register of Santa Maria a Vico, free on Antenati, records Andrea Vigliotti, born 30 November 1853 on Strada Rusciano, the same street where Vincenzo was born 32 years later. His parents were Crescenzo Vigliotti, son of Agostino, a farmer, and Maria Rosa Carfora. He is very probably Vincenzo's father.

finds.headline: A probable birth for Vincenzo's mother, Mariantonia Ruotolo, 1856
finds.summary: The 1856 Santa Maria a Vico births include Maria Antonia Ruotolo, born 28 June 1856 on Strada Rusciano, the same street as Vincenzo and Andrea, to Giuseppe Ruotolo and Angela Vigliotti. The 18 February 1883 marriage names those same parents and gives the bride's age as 27, which fits 1856 by year subtraction, so this is now probable. A later note on her birth act records a marriage to an Alfonso P. in 1896, or possibly 1876; that remarriage has not been located (1896 act 40 and 1876 act 40 are not matches).

finds.headline: Andrea Vigliotti and Mariantonia Ruotolo married at Santa Maria a Vico in 1883
finds.summary: Santa Maria a Vico, Atti di Matrimonio 1883, act 3, records the marriage of Andrea Vigliotti and Mariantonia Ruotolo. The date is read as 18 February 1883; the word Diciotto is uncertain, so the day is flagged. Andrea, 35, a farm worker, is named as the son of Crescenzo and Carfora Mariarosa, both apparently living. Mariantonia, 27, a farm worker, is named as the daughter of Giuseppe and Vigliotti Angela, both apparently living. Those parent names support Andrea's 1853 birth (still probable, because the groom's age implies about 1848) and Mariantonia's 1856 birth (now probable).

finds.headline: Family papers add Margaret Farrell's line and a set of Walsh newspaper clippings
finds.summary: Six photographs of a family-history packet, provided on 26 and 27 November 2026, include published clippings about John J. Walsh and Justice William A. Walsh Jr., a compiled biography of John J., and a compiled account of Margaret Farrell and her parents. Private letters in the same packet are held back from the public site.

finds.headline: John J. Walsh's 1946 obituary names his mother as Margaret Farrell
finds.summary: A family-held clipping of the 18 December 1946 Herald Statesman says John J. Walsh died the day before at St. John's Riverside Hospital, Yonkers, aged 86, a son of Michael Walsh, building contractor, and the former Margaret Farrell, and a brother of William A. Walsh, former Mayor and former City Manager, and of Thomas A. Walsh. Burial was at Saint Joseph's Cemetery. This is the first contemporary newspaper statement in hand that names Margaret Farrell as Michael's wife and John's mother.

finds.headline: A family report names Margaret Farrell's parents and six children
finds.summary: The compiled report says Margaret Farrell was the daughter of John Farrell and Morna Fitzgerald, who came from Ireland to Yonkers about 1844, that she was born about 1842, married Michael Walsh on 22 November 1857 at St. Mary's Church in Yonkers, and died on 5 November 1873, aged 31. It lists six children: John J., James F., Thomas A., Catherine C., Michael A., and William A. Those compiled dates remain family tradition until a register, a civil record, or a photograph of her stone is read. Saint Joseph's Cemetery was not purchased until 1877, so a 1873 burial there is not pinned on the map.

finds.headline: Ellen E. Kelly is probably Michael Walsh's later wife, not William's mother
finds.summary: Earlier site text treated Ellen E. Kelly, the wife named in Michael Walsh's 1916 obituary, as the probable mother of William Aloysius Walsh. The 1946 obituary of John J. Walsh names Margaret Farrell as John's mother, and a family report says Margaret died on 5 November 1873, two years after William's birth in 1871. The best reading is that Margaret was the first wife and is probably William's mother, and that Ellen was a later wife who survived Michael. Agnes Florence Walsh, born in 1889, is probably Ellen's daughter. An 1871 birth or baptism record for William is still needed to settle the maternal link.

finds.headline: A Yonkers Historical Society citation to Judge William A. Walsh, about the summer of 1963
finds.summary: A family-held editorial praises a Yonkers Historical Society citation to Judge Walsh, the first of what it intended as an annual award, and says he was approaching his 92nd birthday that summer. No newspaper name or date is printed on the clipping. For William Aloysius Walsh, born 18 August 1871, a 92nd birthday in the summer would fall in 1963.

finds.headline: William A. Walsh Jr. was sworn in as a State Supreme Court justice
finds.summary: A family-held clipping, datelined White Plains, describes the induction of Justice William A. Walsh Jr. after his election the previous November to a 14-year term. It calls him a former Yonkers city manager and a judge of the Family and County Courts, and names his father, William A. Walsh Sr., as a former city manager, mayor and judge. An official listing gives his first elected or appointed date as 3 November 1970, which would place the ceremony about January 1971, though no date is printed on the clipping. Social Security records already named him as a son of William A. Walsh and Clara Hingston, born in Yonkers on 10 May 1914, and gave his death as 30 January 1999.

finds.headline: John J. Walsh married Annie Fegan in 1880, according to a family note
finds.summary: A typed note in the family papers says John J. Walsh married Annie Fegan in 1880 at St. Joseph's Church in Yonkers, that they had a son, Harry F. Walsh, and a daughter, Margaret, later Mrs. Charles R. Brown, and that Annie died in 1929. A volunteer memorial uses the spelling Ann Fagan Walsh, 1861 to 1929. Fegan and Fagan are treated as variants. The marriage remains family tradition until the register is read. Their children are named in the 1946 obituary but are not added as full profiles in this pass.

finds.headline: Stand-in cards for Michael Walsh's parents, whose names are not yet known
finds.summary: These cards are stand-ins. No record in hand names Michael Walsh's parents. They are on the tree so both of his wives, Margaret Farrell and Ellen E. Kelly, can sit in his family on the canvas.

finds.headline: Vincenzo's World War I draft card index: born 5 July 1885, Scarsdale Avenue
finds.summary: The 1917 to 1918 draft index lists Vincenzo Vigliotti on Scarsdale Avenue in Westchester County, Draft Board 6, born 5 July 1885. It differs by a day from the Italian birth act, which gives 4 July. The card image has not yet been read at card resolution.

finds.headline: The 1917 to 1918 draft card names a relative, Vicenza Vigliotti, so the couple were probably married by then
finds.summary: The index names Vicenza Vigliotti as his relative. This is probably Vincenza Guida as his wife, which would put the marriage before the 1917 or 1918 registration. It does not prove the 31 July 1916 date from a member tree, and no marriage record has been found yet.

finds.headline: Vincenzo's 1942 draft card index: 7 July 1885, with "Buffalo, Italy" as an indexing slip
finds.summary: The 1942 "old man's" draft index lists Vincenzo Vigliotti of Scarsdale, born 7 July 1885, with the birthplace indexed as Buffalo, Italy. His son Vincent Jr. is the next of kin. The Italian birth act, 4 July 1885, still decides his birth date.

finds.headline: A Giovanni Vigliotti married Evelina Golia at Tuckahoe on 29 October 1916, a possible relative of Vincenzo
finds.summary: The state index names the groom Giovanni Vigliotti, the bride Evelina Golia, Tuckahoe, 29 October 1916, certificate 37504. The index entry is certain. Whether Giovanni is a relative of Vincenzo is not proven; they share a surname, the Tuckahoe and Eastchester area and the same period.

finds.headline: A Giovanni John Vigliotti, born 1894, has next of kin Evelyn, which could be Evelina Golia
finds.summary: Born 5 February 1894 in Italy and living in the Bronx in 1942, with next of kin Evelyn Vigliotti. This could be the 1916 Tuckahoe groom, but nothing on the index proves it.

finds.headline: William A. Walsh Jr.'s 1940 draft card confirms his birth: 10 May 1914, Yonkers
finds.summary: He registered at Yonkers on 16 October 1940, aged 26, born 10 May 1914 at Yonkers. This agrees with the Social Security record already used for him.

finds.headline: John J. Walsh's death certificate number: 74279, Yonkers, 17 December 1946
finds.summary: The state death index lists John J Walsh, aged 86, died at Yonkers on 17 December 1946, certificate 74279. It agrees with his 1946 obituary and his son-of-Michael-and-Margaret record.

finds.headline: Thomas A. Walsh in the 1930 census: Buena Vista Avenue, Yonkers, aged 66
finds.summary: A Thomas A Walsh, aged 66 and born in New York, heads a household on Buena Vista Avenue in Yonkers. He is probably Michael Walsh's son. The record is reported to list a wife Mary E and Irish-born parents. A search card suggests he was born in 1863, died on 19 March 1948 and was the son of Michael Walsh and Margaret Farrell; that card has not been opened.

finds.headline: William A. Walsh was elected captain of the Notre Dame football team in 1895
finds.summary: A short wire item says William A Walsh of Yonkers was unanimously elected captain of the Notre Dame football team. A Wikipedia article on the Yonkers mayor says he played football at Notre Dame, so the match is probable. This is the first contemporary newspaper item for him in the file.

finds.headline: William A. Walsh was City Judge of Yonkers in 1917 and lost his seat to William F. Bleakley
finds.summary: On 28 October 1917 The Sun names William A. Walsh as City Judge of Yonkers. On 7 November it reports that William F. Bleakley defeated City Judge William A. Walsh in the election. This matches Wikipedia's account of the same year.

finds.headline: William A. Walsh was Corporation Counsel of Yonkers by September 1919
finds.summary: The Sun reports Corporation Counsel William A. Walsh of Yonkers in court over the Federal Sugar Refining Company tax assessment. This fits the corporation counsel years given by Wikipedia.

finds.headline: A 1942 wire story: a hoaxer sent six prominent men to Yonkers City Hall in Manager Walsh's name
finds.summary: A news filler about William A. Walsh, Yonkers manager, shows him in office in October 1942, and tells how an impersonator phoned in his name and summoned six of the most prominent men in town to City Hall for appointments.

finds.headline: Vincenza's father Alfonso Guida probably crossed to New York in October 1900
finds.summary: An Alfonso Guida, aged 34, married, of Aninzo (probably Arienzo), arrived on the Burgundia on 2 October 1900. His age and town fit the Alfonso who registered the twins in 1899, but the manifest has not been read, so the match is probable. It opens the question of whether he lived in America before his wife died in 1904.

finds.headline: Other Vigliotti men from Santa Maria a Vico reached New York in 1903 and 1911, possible relatives
finds.summary: A Vincenzo Vigliotti, aged 22, of S. Maria a Vico arrived on 20 March 1903, twelve days before our Vincenzo; a Giovanni Vigliotti, aged 26, of the same town arrived in November 1911. No record links either man to Vincenzo, so they stay leads for relatives who may have helped him settle.
